arxiv-2102-00457.title: MultiRocket: Multiple pooling operators and transformations for fast and effective time series classification Thanks: This research has been supported by Australian Research Council grant DP210100072.
arxiv-2102-00457.creator: Chang Wei Tan, Angus Dempster, Christoph Bergmeir, Geoffrey I. Webb
arxiv-2102-00457.description: Abstract We propose MultiRocket, a fast time series classification (TSC) algorithm that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with a tiny fraction of the time and without the complex ensembling structure of many state-of-the-art methods. MultiRocket improves on MiniRocket, one of the fastest TSC algorithms to date, by adding multiple pooling operators and transformations to improve the diversity of the features generated.

arxiv-2104-03960.title: Modulated Periodic Activations for Generalizable Local Functional Representations
arxiv-2104-03960.creator: Ishit Mehta, Michaël Gharbi, Connelly Barnes, Eli Shechtman, Ravi Ramamoorthi, Manmohan Chandraker
arxiv-2104-03960.description: Abstract Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) make powerful functional representations for sampling and reconstruction problems involving low-dimensional signals like images, shapes and light fields. Recent works have significantly improved their ability to represent high-frequency content by using periodic activations or positional encodings. This often came at the expense of generalization: modern methods are typically optimized for a single signal.

arxiv-2107-09749.title: Evaluating Effectiveness of Public Health Intervention Strategies for Mitigating COVID-19 Pandemic
arxiv-2107-09749.creator: Shanghong Xie, Wenbo Wang, Qinxia Wang, Yuanjia Wang, Donglin Zeng
arxiv-2107-09749.description: Abstract Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic is an unprecedented global public health challenge. In the United States (US), state governments have implemented various non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), such as physical distance closure (lockdown), stay-at-home order, mandatory facial mask in public in response to the rapid spread of COVID-19.

arxiv-2204-10835.title: The impact of time-dependent stellar activity on exoplanet atmospheres 2021 The impact of time-dependent stellar activity on exoplanet atmospheres – References
arxiv-2204-10835.creator: Amy J. Louca, Yamila Miguel, Shang-Min Tsai, Cynthia S. Froning, R. O. Parke Loyd, Kevin France
arxiv-2204-10835.description: Abstract M-dwarfs are thought to be hostile environments for exoplanets. Stellar events are very common on such stars. These events might cause the atmospheres of exoplanets to change significantly over time. It is not only the major stellar flare events that contribute to this disequilibrium, but the smaller flares might also affect the atmospheres in an accumulating manner.

arxiv-2311-09593.title: Multi-Step Dialogue Workflow Action Prediction
arxiv-2311-09593.creator: Ramya Ramakrishnan Ethan R. Elenberg Hashan Narangodage Ryan McDonald
arxiv-2311-09593.description: Abstract In task-oriented dialogue, a system often needs to follow a sequence of actions, called a workflow , that complies with a set of guidelines in order to complete a task. In this paper, we propose the novel problem of multi-step workflow action prediction, in which the system predicts multiple future workflow actions.

arxiv-2402-10457.title: Learning-Augmented Search Data Structures
arxiv-2402-10457.creator: Chunkai Fu, Brandon G. Nguyen, Jung Hoon Seo, Ryan Zesch, Samson Zhou
arxiv-2402-10457.description: Abstract We study the integration of machine learning advice to improve upon traditional data structure designed for efficient search queries. Although there has been recent effort in improving the performance of binary search trees using machine learning advice, e.g., Lin et. al.

arxiv-2504-00424.title: Hawkeye : Efficient Reasoning with Model Collaboration
arxiv-2504-00424.creator: Jianshu She, Zhuohao Li, Zhemin Huang, Qi Li, Peiran Xu, Haonan Li, Qirong Ho
arxiv-2504-00424.description: Abstract Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in enhancing the reasoning abilities of large language models (LLMs). However, its efficiency remains a challenge due to the generation of excessive intermediate reasoning tokens, which introduce semantic redundancy and overly detailed reasoning steps.

arxiv-2504-05917.title: Indexing Strings with Utilities
arxiv-2504-05917.creator: Giulia Bernardini, Huiping Chen, Alessio Conte, Roberto Grossi, Veronica Guerrini, Grigorios Loukides, Nadia Pisanti, Solon P. Pissis
arxiv-2504-05917.description: Abstract Applications in domains ranging from bioinformatics to advertising feature strings (sequences of letters over some alphabet) that come with numerical scores ( utilities ). The utilities quantify the importance, interest, profit, or risk of the letters occurring at every position of a string. For instance, DNA fragments generated by sequencing machines come with a confidence score per position.

pmc-11328395.title: Move-PCD—a multi-center longitudinal randomized controlled superiority trial on the effect of a 6-month individualized supported physical activity (PA) program on quality of life (QoL) in children, adolescents, and adults with primary ciliary dyskinesia
pmc-11328395.creator: Anna Teresa Hoffmann, Anna Mai, Klaus Baum, Anne Schlegtendal, Christoph Maier, Julien Stein, Marianne Tokic, Stefanie Dillenhöfer, Thomas Lücke, Nina Timmesfeld, Folke Brinkmann
pmc-11328395.description: BackgroundPrimary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare genetical disease with malfunction of the motile cilia leading to impaired muco-ciliary clearance in the respiratory tract. There is no cure for PCD, only supportive therapy aimed at minimizing the progression of the disease and improving the patient’s quality of life (QoL).

pmc-11709398.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Brain Structural and Antipsychotic Drug Dosage in BPSD
pmc-11709398.creator: Bo Hong, Tianli Tao, Han Zhang, Xia Li, Jianhua Chen, Ling Yue
pmc-11709398.description: BackgroundPsychotropic medications are commonly prescribed for behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD). However, the safety of antipsychotic drugs has always been a concern. The study aims to investigate the relationship between brain structural and the effective dosage of antipsychotic drugs.MethodAll the subjects were from Shanghai Mental Health Center.

pmc-12441051.title: Laboratory preparation methods for human-derived fecal microbial suspensions for fecal microbiota transplantation: a review and standardization perspectives
pmc-12441051.creator: Jinhua Gong, Yuchi Liu, Liuye Huang
pmc-12441051.description: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has advanced significantly as a therapeutic approach over the past few decades. Preparing fecal suspensions for FMT is one of the key steps. However, there is no unified standard or recognized procedure for preparing fecal suspensions in laboratories.

pmc-12577343.title: Mid-term outcomes of paclitaxel-coated balloon for de novo non-small coronary lesions: a pooled analysis
pmc-12577343.creator: Xingqiang He, Yi Liu, Zhiyong Yin, Fei Li, Robert-Jan van Geuns, Scot Garg, Yoshinobu Onuma, Patrick W. Serruys, Chao Gao, Ling Tao
pmc-12577343.description: BackgroundThe efficacy of drug-coated balloons (DCB) for the treatment of de novo, non-small coronary lesions remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world performance of DCB-only angioplasty in this setting.MethodsPatients with de novo, non-small coronary lesions (≥ 2.5 mm) treated exclusively with either drug-eluting stents (DES) or DCB were included from the DCB registry and two DES registries.

pmc-12618693.title: Structures of CRP antigen-antibody complexes provide insights into the mechanism of specific recognition
pmc-12618693.creator: Yijian Li, Qianxi Yu, Mengtan Du, Jian Zhang, Tonggong Liu, Jingzhe Wang, Qingchun Wei, Yong Peng, Chaohui Duan, Dayong Gu, Fuxing Zeng
pmc-12618693.description: Antigen-antibody specific recognition constitutes fundamental research in molecular drug design and immune diagnostics, where cumulative non-covalent interactions critically determine binding affinities. Current mechanistic understanding of antibody affinity optimization remains incomplete, hindering rational structure-based design of therapeutic antibodies and bispecific variants.

pmc-12623417.title: Experimental verification and comparative analysis of peak expiratory flow measuring devices
pmc-12623417.creator: Concepción Paz, Eduardo Suárez, Alberto Fernández-Villar, Elena Puga
pmc-12623417.description: This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking of six commercially available peak expiratory flow meters (PFMs), using a precise experimental spirometric test bench. Eight peak expiratory flows (PEF) ranging from 59.40 to 688.80 L/min at three frequencies, were systematically applied to each device.

pmc-12981272.title: The dynamics of glycosylation in trophoblast cells: development, function, and pregnancy-related disorders
pmc-12981272.creator: Tiantong Wang, Yan Wang, Yilun Wu, Yi Zhang, Fang Ma
pmc-12981272.description: BackgroundTrophoblast cells are essential for embryo implantation and placental development, with their functional versatility critically regulated by dynamic glycosylation modifications. These post-translational modifications create a spatiotemporally-defined molecular code that directs trophoblast behavior throughout pregnancy, though its comprehensive role in both physiological and pathological contexts remains to be fully elucidated.DiscussionGlycosylation orchestrates key trophoblast functions in a stage-specific manner.

pmc-13265483.title: Tracking the dynamic breakdown of contextual coherence in schizophrenia using language models
pmc-13265483.creator: Seunghyong Ryu, Ju-Wan Kim, Min Jhon, Young-Chul Chung, Seok Jun Kim, Suehyun Lee, Jae-Min Kim, Sung-Wan Kim
pmc-13265483.description: Disorganized speech is a core clinical feature of schizophrenia, reflecting disruptions in contextual integration. To objectively quantify the unfolding nature of natural speech, this study investigated the dynamic temporal trajectory of contextual coherence breakdown using sequential surprisal derived from autoregressive language models. We analyzed transcripts from 249 patients with schizophrenia and 159 matched healthy controls across eight diverse speech tasks.

pmc-13361189.title: Atypical Bilateral Iris Transillumination without Pigment Dispersion: A Case Report Suggestive of BAIT
pmc-13361189.creator: Maura Mancini, Claudio Brancato, Alessandro Meduri, Gregorio Lo Giudice
pmc-13361189.description: IntroductionBilateral Acute Iris Transillumination (BAIT) is a rare ocular condition characterized by acute iris depigmentation, pigment dispersion in the anterior chamber, sphincter paralysis, and frequently elevated intraocular pressure. However, atypical presentations may occur, complicating diagnosis and expanding the clinical spectrum of the disease.Case PresentationA 25-year-old woman presented with acute onset of severe photophobia associated with migraine and visual aura.
